purpose: Test the first higher-domain holographic normal forms against the exact ordered arity-6 GF(3) current signature from v8.5.2. Use only tensor flattening-rank invariants that remain valid under arbitrary invertible basis changes on individual ports; do not incorrectly apply a symmetric-Holant dichotomy to this non-symmetric signature.

canonical_local_signature.domain: GF(3) on six ordered exposed-current ports [L0,L2,L3,R0,R2,R3]
canonical_local_signature.conservation: sum_i k_i = 0 mod 3 in the all-outgoing local orientation
canonical_local_signature.value: F6(k)=0 off conservation; on conservation F6(k)=-2+3*delta(VP dot k=0)+3*delta(VM dot k=0)
canonical_local_signature.orientation_note: Changing the orientation of one physical current edge is the invertible local domain permutation k->-k. Such per-leg invertible changes preserve every flattening rank used by this barrier.

non_symmetry_firewall.witness: F6(0,1,0,0,0,2)=-2 but swapping the first two ports gives F6(1,0,0,0,0,2)=1.
non_symmetry_firewall.consequence: The real-domain-3 Holant* dichotomy of Cai-Ihm 2025 is a theorem for symmetric signatures. It is used here only as motivation for concrete normal forms; it is NOT invoked to conclude #P-hardness for F6 or for the restricted smooth-Hamiltonian JANUS source class.

exact_flattening_invariants.one_vs_five: All six 1|5 flattenings have exact rank 3 over Q.
exact_flattening_invariants.profile: rank 6 occurs twice, rank 9 four times, rank 12 four times
exact_flattening_invariants.invariance: For any bipartition A|B, applying arbitrary invertible matrices independently on the six tensor legs multiplies the flattening on the left and right by invertible Kronecker products. Therefore its matrix rank is unchanged.

barrier_theorem.name: NO_LOCAL_INVERTIBLE_BASIS_TO_LOW_RANK_OR_TWO_PLUS_ONE_DOMAIN_SEPARATED_NORMAL_FORM_V8_5_6
claims: No product of invertible per-port 3x3 basis changes can map F6 to a tensor of CP/tensor rank at most 3. Every such tensor has every bipartition flattening rank at most 3, while F6 has 3|3 rank 12.

In particular this excludes the GenEQ / three-pure-tensor higher-domain normal form a*u^tensor6+b*v^tensor6+c*w^tensor6, even allowing independent local invertible bases stronger than one common orthogonal basis.

No product of invertible per-port 3x3 basis changes can map F6 to support contained in {B,G}^6 union {R}^6. Across a 3|3 cut the {B,G} block has rank at most 2^3=8 and the singleton R^6 term contributes at most one more rank, so every such tensor has rank at most 9; F6 has rank 12.
The 1|5 rank 3 also excludes support entirely inside a fixed two-element subdomain after any local invertible basis change, since such support has one-leg mode rank at most 2.
barrier_theorem.scope: This is a local normal-form obstruction, not a generic Holant hardness theorem and not a proof that every nonsymmetric domain-3 holographic or graph-structural contraction is impossible.

exact_controls.non_symmetry_witness: swap(0,1) changes the frozen tensor entry from -2 to 1

external_context.paper: Jin-Yi Cai and Jin Soo Ihm, Holant* Dichotomy on Domain Size 3: A Geometric Perspective, ICALP 2025, LIPIcs 334:148.
external_context.relevant_fact: For real-valued symmetric domain-3 signatures, the dichotomy is expressed through orthogonal holographic transforms and tractable geometric normal forms. In the single-signature higher-arity analysis, the tractable forms have tensor decompositions with at most three pure powers after an orthogonal transform. The present F6 is non-symmetric, so only the concrete geometric forms—not the hardness conclusion—are tested here.

anti_loop.v8_5_5: No row-space memoization or MacWilliams duality is used; those routes are frozen by v8.5.5.
